description:
Location: `crate-jmap-base-client/src/request.rs:99-143`

  #[non_exhaustive]
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub struct Session {
      ...
      /// Username associated with the current credentials (RFC 8620 §2).
      pub username: String,
      ...
      /// Opaque session state token (RFC 8620 §2).
      pub state: State,
  }

CONCERN
`Session` is the RFC 8620 §2 session object returned from `.well-known/jmap`. It derives `Debug` with two fields that are sensitivity-adjacent:

1. `username` (line 116) — the authenticated user's identifier. For most JMAP deployments this is a full email address. Per privacy frameworks (GDPR Article 4, CCPA §1798.140) this is PII; logs containing it are subject to retention and access-control obligations. The `derive(Debug)` means any `{:?}`-format of a Session writes the email to the output stream.

2. `state` (line 142) — the opaque session state token. RFC 8620 §2 says clients use this for cache validation; it is NOT an auth credential, but it is the server-side identifier for the client's session and uniquely identifies it. Logging it lets an operator pivot from log → request-trace → user, which is the same shape of leak as logging a session cookie.

This is the same class as the closed JMAP-sc1b.79 finding (BearerAuth/BasicAuth Debug redaction). `.79` only covered the two AuthProvider impls; `Session` and the dereived-Debug shape was missed.

WHAT GOES WRONG
Privacy / PII exposure. Operator logs that Debug-print a Session value (any `tracing::debug!("session: {:?}", session)` call, or a panic with the Session in scope) leak the user's identity. Indirect: aids correlation attacks against pseudo-anonymous logs.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Remove `Debug` from the derive list at line 100.
2. Add a manual Debug impl that redacts `username` and shows only `state.fingerprint()` or 'state: [opaque]' rather than the full state value. Mirror the BearerAuth shape at `crate-jmap-base-client/src/auth.rs:183-189`.
3. Add a regression test that constructs a Session with a canary username and asserts the canary does not appear in `{:?}` output (mirror `auth.rs:443-475` pattern).
4. Apply the same treatment to `AccountInfo` if it has similarly PII-adjacent fields (left as a follow-up; check `crate-jmap-base-client/src/request.rs` for sibling types).

ORACLE
- Closed JMAP-sc1b.79 — the in-repo precedent for Debug redaction + canary test on credential/PII-bearing types.
- RFC 8620 §2 — defines Session.username as the authenticated principal; §1.4 defines State as opaque to clients but inherently server-side identifying.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P3. Hygiene / privacy defense-in-depth. The current code doesn't actively log it; the risk is the next contributor who adds a tracing call.
title: Security: Session derives Debug exposing username (PII) and session state token (crate-jmap-base-client/src/request.rs:100-143)
